newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Peasants decide to oust farm minister.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Peasants decide to oust farm minister.

text.p: The Polish Peasant Party (PSL), smaller partner in the ruling coalition, said it decided on Wednesday to sack its agriculture minister Roman Jagielinski for failing to safeguard farmers' interests.

But Jagielinski, who has been exposed in his party since he unsuccessfully challenged Waldemar Pawlak for its leadership last year, said he would not quit and his removal was now up to Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz of the larger, ex-communist, Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) party.

The PSL's executive committee said in a statement that it wanted Jagielinski, who is also deputy prime minister, to be replaced in both roles by a fellow PSL parliamentary deputy, Jaroslaw Kalinowski, 35.

"The Supreme Executive Council of the PSL, taking into account the situation in agriculture and the food economy, withdraws our colleague Roman Jagielinski from the functions of deputy prime minister and agriculture minister," it said.
But a surprised Jagielinski told reporters: "I don't intend to offer my resignation as I do not consider that this decision has any concrete justification."
Peasant party spokesman Aleksander Bentkowski told a news conference it did not expect Cimoszewicz to oppose its decision about a ministry which was at its disposal under the parties' coalition pact.
Last week Cimoszewicz replaced Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko with Marek Belka, without consulting the PSL, arguing that the finance portfolio was the SLD's to fill.

Many party colleagues say Jagielinski, a large landowner, is more concerned with the priorities of the ex-communists, over issues including the need for fast entry into the European Union, than with the plight of the host of small farmers who make up PSL ranks.

One Western diplomat told Reuters the Peasant party could now tell any disillusioned supporters, during campaigning for parliamentary elections due in September, that Jagielinski was to blame for any shortcomings in coalition farm policies.
The Peasant pary, which might form a coalition with rightist parties if the ex-communists lose the elctions, want to distance themselves from their larger partner.

The PSL statement said Jagielinski was being sacked for taking decisions which led to a Polish food and commodities trade deficit of $1 billion last year and for inadequate market interventions causing livestock prices to fall.
